newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Creditanstalt still not seen up to European banks.
newsitem.headline: Creditanstalt still not seen up to European banks.

text.p: A rise in Creditanstalt's 1996 earnings was broadly in line with market expectations but the Austrian bank still had some way to go before it measures up to its main European competitors, analysts said on Thursday.
"Their operating performance is not so bad, but their evaluation is not stunning compared to other European banks," said James Alexander, Austria analyst at Kleinwort Benson in London.

Austria's second biggest bank, due to be privatised, posted a rise in net profit to a preliminary 2.6 billion schillings from 2.166 billion in 1995, while operating profit climbed to 6.2 billion from 6.14 billion a year ago.
Clare Fargeot, analyst at James Capel in London said there appeared to be a discrepancy in the calculation of net and operating profit level figures.

"Everything seems to be moving along nicely at the operating level but there seems to be a lot of fudging that's gone on between operating and the net profit levels because it's much higher than what the market was going for."
Final bids for the sale of the state's 70 percent stake in the bank are due at 0800 GMT on Friday.
"It looks like they're squeezing all that they can out to paint a pretty picture (ahead of the sale)," Fargeot said, noting the figures looked better at face value than they were fundamentally.
Roland Neuwirth at Deutsche Bank in Austria said the results were "mildly positive" and in line with his estimates, but would not have any effect on the sale.
"The results have nothing to do with the sale of Creditanstalt. No one will improve their offer on the basis of the figures," he said.
"There is still scope for further improving the efficiency and profitability of the bank," Neuwirth added.
James Capel's Fargeot was more critical:
"The return on capital that it generates is a good five percentage short of what the Swiss are generating so it is pretty unprofitable compared to the other European banks."
The bank said its return on equity had risen to about 10 percent in 1996, from 8.6 percent in 1995.
Shares in Creditanstalt were among the biggest decliners on the Vienna bourse on Thursday, in spite of the earnings rise posted earlier.

Creditanstalt ordinary shares ended 5.1 schillings lower at 482.9 on heavy volume. The bank's widely-held preferred shares were down 7.9 schillings at 716.1. -- Elizabeth Fullerton, Vienna newsroom, +431 531 12257
